title: nano on servers
summary: Edit root-owned files safely, keep backups, and make nano (or vim) the editor every tool opens.

steps.title: Editing files you do not own
body: `nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config` as a normal user opens the file read-only in practice: `^O` fails with `Permission denied`. Two fixes:
```text
sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config     # runs the whole editor as root
sudoedit /etc/ssh/sshd_config      # better: copies the file to a temp file, runs YOUR editor as you,
# then copies it back as root when you exit
`sudoedit` (same as `sudo -e`) is safer: your editor and its plugins never run as root.
Useful flags on a server:
```text
nano -B file    # keep a backup as file~ when saving
nano -l file    # show line numbers (handy when an error says "line 42")
nano -v file    # view only: you cannot change anything
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: Match the command to what it does.
pairs: edit a root file with your editor running as you

steps.prompt: Why is nano often the right choice when you write instructions for a colleague on a production server?
options: What they type goes straight into the file and the exit keys are printed on screen, so a nervous typist cannot get stuck in a mode
It is faster than vim for every task
It is installed on every container image
steps.explain: nano is modeless and self-documenting. It is not everywhere (minimal images often have only `vi`, or nothing), which is why you learn vi too.

steps.title: EDITOR and VISUAL
body: `git commit`, `crontab -e`, `visudo`, `sudoedit`, `kubectl edit` and many others open "your editor". They look at environment variables:
```text
export VISUAL=nano     # preferred, full-screen editor
export EDITOR=nano     # fallback
Put the lines in `~/.bashrc` (or `~/.zshrc`) to make them permanent. Debian and Ubuntu also have a system-wide default: `sudo update-alternatives --config editor`.
git checks, in order: `GIT_EDITOR`, the `core.editor` setting, `VISUAL`, `EDITOR`, then falls back to `vi`. That fallback is why so many people meet vim for the first time in the middle of a commit.

steps.prompt: Make nano the editor for every tool in this and future shells.
steps.explain: `export` puts the variable in the environment of programs you start.

steps.prompt: Order the places git looks for an editor, first checked at the top.

steps.title: ~/.nanorc
body: nano reads `~/.nanorc` at start-up. A good server-friendly one:
```text
set linenumbers      # line numbers on the left
set tabsize 4
set tabstospaces     # Tab inserts spaces (YAML hates tabs)
set autoindent       # new lines keep the indentation
set backup           # like -B
include "/usr/share/nano/*.nanorc"   # syntax colouring

steps.title: Which editor will git open?
prompt: Write `string GitEditor(Dictionary<string, string> env, string? coreEditor)` returning the editor git uses:
2. otherwise `coreEditor` if not null or empty,
3. otherwise `VISUAL`, then `EDITOR` (each only if present and not empty),
Treat a value that is only whitespace as empty.
starter: string GitEditor(Dictionary<string, string> env, string? coreEditor)
solution: string GitEditor(Dictionary<string, string> env, string? coreEditor)
string? Get(string name) => env.TryGetValue(name, out var v) && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(v) ? v : null;
hints: Write a small local function that returns the variable or null.
template: Dojo.Eq("nothing set falls back to vi", "vi", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string>(), null));
Dojo.Eq("EDITOR is used", "nano", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["EDITOR"] = "nano" }, null));
Dojo.Eq("VISUAL beats EDITOR", "vim", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["EDITOR"] = "nano", ["VISUAL"] = "vim" }, null));
Dojo.Eq("core.editor beats VISUAL", "code --wait", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["VISUAL"] = "vim" }, "code --wait"));
Dojo.Eq("GIT_EDITOR beats everything", "nano", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["GIT_EDITOR"] = "nano", ["VISUAL"] = "vim" }, "emacs"));
Dojo.Eq("empty values are skipped", "nano", GitEditor(new Dictionary<string, string> { ["GIT_EDITOR"] = " ", ["EDITOR"] = "nano" }, ""));
